what_was_done: cd's option words (-P, -L, -e, ...) are skipped and '--' ends the options, so the first operand decides the later wheres ('cd -P /tmp && git status' now gives /tmp, 'cd -- sub' /base/sub, 'cd -- -P' the literal /base/-P, an option-only cd gives '' because it goes home). pushd and popd set the later wheres to '' (the directory stack decides; never guessed). A for or case reserved word now marks its segment opaque, so the loop variable is no longer read as the program ('for f in a b; do rm -rf $f; done': header opaque, body program rm). Verified by mutation: reverting the cd branch fails test_where_unknown_forms.

The coverage check is factored into gate_case_problems(rows, table) and the modules-to-rows check into module_row_problems(rows, rules_dir); test_gate_case_coverage calls both over registry.RULES (vacuous-safe while RULES is empty). A case's module is compared against the module the row actually loads (entry.module or 'vsdd.rules.' + id with dashes as underscores), so a defaulted row no longer reads as ''. module_row_problems faults a vsdd/rules/*.py file with no row and a row whose module is not a vsdd.rules file. Both are tested with hand-built RuleEntry rows: an uncovered gate row, a covered one, a case naming a defaulted module, a straying module, an orphaned module file, and a row with no file — each caught by mutation, since the empty live loop alone proves nothing.
where: next/tests/hooks/test_rule_cases.py (loaded_module, gate_case_problems, module_row_problems); tests: next/tests/hooks/test_rule_cases.py::test_gate_case_problems_catches_gaps, test_modules_match_rows, test_gate_case_coverage

Two caller tests. test_marker_is_staged_outside_calls spies on os.replace and asserts the staged file sits under <root>/.factory/local/hooks/tmp/ as <key>.json.tmp before landing in calls/ — this is the test that fails when the staging moves back into calls/. test_replace_failure_leaves_no_tmp_in_calls makes os.replace raise (a kill before the rename): the call blocks with caller_marker_unwritable and calls/ holds no *.tmp file. All three verified by mutation.

main._recent_rule_faults now matches event types through the model.py constants EVENT_RULE_ERROR and EVENT_RULE_TIMEOUT instead of the literals 'rule.error' and 'rule.timeout' — the quarantine no longer breaks silently if a constant is renamed. main._events_dir delegates to a shared _events_dir_of(env, root), the same resolver the bad-input path uses.

Settled on: arithmetic is opaque only when it nests a command substitution. _read_word distinguishes '$((' from '$(': an arithmetic span sets word.subst only when its interior ('$(', '`') holds a command substitution or a backtick, in the bare and the double-quoted forms alike; _own_opacity's '$((' exclusion is no longer dead code but the other half of the same decision, and the module and _Word docstrings say so. 'echo $((1+2))', quoted 'n=$((1+2))' and a vsdd call with an arithmetic argument stay judgeable, so the caller marker survives; '$(($(wc -l)+1))' and a backtick inside the arithmetic are opaque. Verified by mutation: forcing subst for arithmetic fails the test.

Bad input in notify and brief now logs rule.error (rule 'runner', code 'runner_bad_input', fail 'open', session id 'unknown'); rule.block stays gate-only; the directory resolution is shared (_events_dir_of) and honours VSDD_EVENTS_DIR in both paths. test_bad_input_logged_in_gate_only now expects one rule.error after notify, two after brief, and rule.block third after gate, with no rule.block outside gate.
